title: Archive one active Client offline through the isolated Client browser

requirements.invariant: One explicit archive action may target only the currently observed active Account-scoped Client and exact revision. Accepted local evidence immediately moves that stable Client from Active to Archived for every shared local consumer, including removal from new-Project selection, while local evidence never grants server authority.

Archiving a Client preserves stable Client identity, every existing Project relationship and all Transfer, Invoice, attachment/media, Item, Transaction, accounting and history evidence. It changes only Client lifecycle, revision and server update time plus immutable operation evidence, and cannot delete, merge, reassign or cascade Projects.

Archive is a distinct history-preserving command, not restore/unarchive, hard delete, rename, merge, Project Client reassignment or cascade. This bounded slice admits only currently observed active Client evidence and requires trusted non-active rejection; it does not decide a broader already-archived resubmission or no-op product policy and does not advance O-025 or O-042/O-043.

The verified ClientArchiveIntent, ClientArchiveUseCase, ArchiveClientCommand, expected-revision precondition, fingerprint, one-call dispatch, receipt validation, cancellation and stable failures remain sole semantic owners; this slice composes them without a lifecycle Boolean or alternate operation contract.

Without network, acceptance atomically records immutable operation evidence, an insert-only archive command and a separate local-only Client lifecycle overlay in the encrypted Principal/Account database; immediate directory/detail and Project-setup eligibility evidence remains explicitly partial and survives close/reopen until rejection or qualifying authoritative readback.

Earlier accepted Client creation and Project setup referencing the Client remain ahead of archive while queued/applying; applied prior Projects are preserved, and exact replay of a Project-setup OperationID accepted before archive resolves before archive-overlay validation. Rejected Client creation unblocks archive for trusted missing/non-active disposition without infinite retry and the overlay remains until authoritative terminal archive evidence; rejected Project setup no longer blocks archive. Transient upload failure retains exact work; applied optimism awaits matching applied evidence and archived or newer authoritative Client readback; stale readback never clears or resurrects optimism.

The complete UInt64 expected revision remains exact command evidence without floating-point coercion. Archive locks an active Client at the exact revision; out-of-signed-range values cannot match, signed-bigint maximum cannot increment, and concurrent same-revision archives yield one apply and one durable conflict. Client archive and Project creation serialize on the same deterministic Client lock: create first may apply before archive and remains preserved; archive first makes later create return durable project_setup_client_not_selectable with no successful post-archive Project and no deadlock.

The trusted handler authenticates first, verifies exact actor, active Account membership and Client-management capability before subject/result disclosure, locks one Account/Client row, validates command/replay/lifecycle/revision, mutates only allowed Client columns and writes one immutable terminal result. The shared result boundary reserves client-archive- for canonical same-Account Client archive only; non-archive commands cannot squat it, and cross-Account/cross-command results cannot disclose or rebind it. Direct Client/result writes and unauthorized or cross-Account reads fail closed.

Archive submission derives only from one exact current selected active Client detail presentation and locally observed revision. Represented partial/stale or cached content remains usable offline; waiting, absence, unavailable, uncached failure, archived, mismatched or stale-selection evidence makes zero calls. The shared Client directory overlay must feed Client browsing and Project Setup so no stale or current post-archive new-Project selection can succeed locally.

Work is confined to ten reserved leaves and frozen shared target touchpoints in the isolated target worktree. Client identity must be client-archive-<sha256(account UTF-8)>-<lowercase canonical UUID> through a generic account-bound identity primitive also adopted by Project archive without changing Project archive bytes. At implementation the non-runnable `.sql.ready` marker CONFIG-2DBC5A626444 remains byte-identical and retired with explicit replacement evidence while separately registered runnable pgTAP leaf CONFIG-86F1E734BC70 replaces it and every planned database-test owner path moves from `.sql.ready` to `.sql` in the same synchronized checkpoint. This adds no restore/delete/rename/merge/reassignment/cascade/accounting/media/preferences/target MCP/source migration/hosted/Firebase/production/release/cutover behavior; A-003/A-004 remain proposed.

Every other Client field, every currently represented Project/related/history row remains byte-identical, no cascade or related write exists, and every later related table must add the same preservation regression.

Missing, non-active, stale/future/out-of-range/exhausted revision and permanent validation yield bounded durable outcomes only after non-enumerating scope authorization; no broad already-archived no-op is claimed.

Membership/capability/Client/result predicates use indexed exact scope paths and stable auth evaluation is hoisted where applicable.
Reuse existing Account-scoped Client, Project and immutable operation-result streams unchanged; archive command/overlay rows never enter download streams as authority.

Add one local-only pending Client archive overlay and one insert-only archive command. Acceptance commits operation/command/overlay atomically in encrypted Account storage without updating synchronized rows.

Use a generic account-bound identity primitive for client-archive and byte-identical Project archive validation. Exact replay resolves before active/effective-revision validation; invalid, stale or non-active bases create no rows.

Earlier queued/applying Client creation and Project setup dependencies stay ahead of archive FIFO; rejected Client creation unblocks archive for authoritative missing/non-active disposition without fabricating a local server result or retrying forever, rejected Project setup unblocks archive, and applied prior Projects remain preserved.

Every shared Client directory/detail consumer immediately projects archived partial evidence; Project Setup removes the option and rejects every new/unaccepted stale or current local operation against effective archived state, but exact replay of a Project-setup OperationID accepted before archive returns its prior receipt before overlay validation.

Transient failure retains work. Durable rejection removes only exact optimism; applied waits for exact archived/newer authoritative readback; stale readback cannot clear/resurrect it. Archive/browser observations and runtime shutdown cancel, join and drain without old-generation mutation.
